import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.Mahler32
/-!
# Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Mahler's Z-numbers

See also FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Mahler32.lean.

*References:*
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10.
  - [Mah68] Mahler, Kurt. "An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2."
    Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society 8.2 (1968): 313-321.
  - [FLP95] Flatto, Leopold, Jeffrey C. Lagarias, and Andrew D. Pollington.
    "On the range of fractional parts $\{\xi(p/q)^n\}$."
    Acta Arithmetica 70.2 (1995): 125-147.
-/

namespace Bugeaud09

/--
Problem 10.9. There are no real numbers $\xi$ such that $0 \le \{\xi (3/2)^n\} < 1/2$
for every positive integer $n$, i.e. no Z-number exists. Posed by Mahler [Mah68].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_9 : type_of% Mahler32.mahler_conjecture := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check: `1` is not a Z-number, since for `n = 1` we have
$\{1 \cdot (3/2)^1\} = \{3/2\} = 1/2 \not< 1/2$.
-/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_isZNumber_one : ¬ IsZNumber 1 := by
  rintro ⟨-, h⟩
  have h1 := h 1 le_rfl
  rw [pow_one, one_mul] at h1
  have hfr : Int.fract (3 / 2 : ℝ) = 1 / 2 := by rw [Int.fract]; norm_num [Int.floor_eq_iff]
  rw [hfr] at h1
  exact lt_irrefl _ h1

/--
Mahler [Mah68] proved that the set of Z-numbers has Lebesgue measure zero.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_9.variants.measure_zero :
    MeasureTheory.volume {ξ : ℝ | IsZNumber ξ} = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
Flatto, Lagarias, and Pollington [FLP95] proved that the set of Z-numbers has
Hausdorff dimension strictly less than $1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_9.variants.dimH_lt_one :
    dimH {ξ : ℝ | IsZNumber ξ} < 1 := by
  sorry

end Bugeaud09

findings.description: The docstring at lines 37–38 says there are no real numbers ξ satisfying the displayed fractional-part inequalities, without requiring ξ > 0. Literally, ξ = 0 satisfies every inequality. The Lean theorem is correct on this point: it elaborates to ∀ x : ℝ, IsZNumber x → False, and IsZNumber includes 0 < x. This is a prose omission, not a defect in the theorem statement. The zero counterexample to the unrestricted prose was verified in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: Mahler [Mah68], p. 313, begins “Let α be an arbitrary positive number” before defining Z-numbers (https://doi.org/10.1017/S1446788700005371). The cited Wikipedia article likewise defines a Z-number as a positive real number: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahler%27s_3/2_problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Change “There are no real numbers ξ” to “There are no positive real numbers ξ”. No change to the Lean statement is needed.

reformulations.difference: Mahler’s original definition quantifies over n ≥ 0, whereas the imported IsZNumber quantifies over n ≥ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let Z₀ be Mahler’s positive-real predicate using all n ≥ 0, and Z₁ be IsZNumber. For every ξ, Z₁(ξ) ↔ Z₀(ξ·3/2), since (ξ·3/2)(3/2)^n = ξ(3/2)^(n+1). Multiplication by 3/2 is a bijection on positive reals, so nonexistence is equivalent under the two conventions. The explicit lower fractional-part bound is automatic from Int.fract_nonneg. The equivalence with the elaborated theorem type was proved in /workspace/review/reindex.lean.

reformulations.difference: The Lean set uses n ≥ 1 rather than the n ≥ 0 convention in Mahler’s paper.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing Z₀ and Z₁ for these sets, Z₀ = (fun ξ => ξ·3/2) '' Z₁. Equivalently, Z₁ is the preimage of Z₀ under this scaling, so volume(Z₁) = (2/3)·volume(Z₀). Consequently their measure-zero statements are equivalent. This was proved as Review.measure_zero_reindex without using any sorry-backed theorem.

reformulations.difference: The Lean set uses n ≥ 1 rather than the n ≥ 0 convention used for generalized Z-numbers in FLP.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two sets differ by multiplication by 3/2, a continuous linear equivalence of ℝ. Such a map preserves Hausdorff dimension. Both equality of the dimensions and equivalence of the bounds dimH < 1 were proved in /workspace/review/reindex.lean.

sources_consulted: Mahler, K. (1968), An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2, pp. 313–321, especially the definition on p. 313 and countability result (11) on p. 315. https://doi.org/10.1017/S1446788700005371 ; full paper read at https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/6416420BFE33A5DDC3DAB6EA358C2B0B/S1446788700005371a.pdf/div-class-title-an-unsolved-problem-on-the-powers-of-3-2-a-href-fn01-ref-type-fn-a-div.pdf

Flatto, L., Lagarias, J. C., and Pollington, A. D. (1995), On the range of fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n}, especially pp. 126–127, Theorem 1.1, and its countability proof. https://doi.org/10.4064/aa-70-2-125-147 ; full paper read at https://www.impan.pl/shop/publication/transaction/download/product/108521?download.pdf
Bugeaud’s author and book pages: https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~bugeaud/ ; https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~bugeaud/Book2.html ; https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~bugeaud/Monog.html

could_not_verify: Bugeaud09.problem_10_9 — exact wording and numbering in Bugeaud’s Problem 10.9 could not be inspected: the public Cambridge preview stops at Problem 10.3 and the full chapter requires access. The mathematical nonexistence claim was independently verified against the separately cited Mahler original and Wikipedia.
review.notes: No substantive mathematical statement defects were found. Mahler’s countability result implies the measure-zero variant and, in fact, Hausdorff dimension zero. FLP Theorem 1.1, specialized to p = 3, q = 2, s = 0, t = 1/2, also gives countability, so the dimension variant is a valid weaker corollary; no equivalence with countability is claimed. The sanity-check proof has no sorry dependency. Additional Lean checks verified exclusion of nonpositive ξ, measurability of the Z-number set, empty-set conventions, and exact rational boundary calculations. The final reindex.lean experiment compiled with zero errors and warnings; all inspected proof dependencies exclude sorryAx.
